finding.leakix.exposed: {count} service(s) reachable without authentication according to LeakIX
leakix.key_rejected: LeakIX key rejected by the service
leakix.score_clean: No leak or open service reported by LeakIX
leakix.unreadable: Unreadable response from the LeakIX service
module.leakix.checks: Queries LeakIX (key required) for data leaks and services exposed without authentication on the domain or address. Credentials found are never copied.
module.leakix.fix:
Remove the exposure right away: for each host and port reported in the result, block access from the Internet (server firewall, security group or your cloud provider's firewall) or stop the service if it is not needed; for a file, backup or status page reachable by URL, remove it from the web server.
If the leak or the open service gave access to credentials, API keys, tokens or a database: assume they were copied, change the passwords, revoke and regenerate the keys, then look in the access logs for unknown connections since the date of the exposure.
Make the service listen only locally (`127.0.0.1`) or on the private network and require authentication: databases (Redis, MongoDB, Elasticsearch, PostgreSQL, MySQL), admin consoles and dashboards must never be open to the Internet (snippet below).
For remote administration (SSH, RDP, web admin interface): restrict access to your fixed IP addresses or go through a VPN, and turn on multi-factor authentication when the service supports it.
If LeakIX reports a known vulnerability (CVE) on a service: update it to a fixed version, or put it behind a reverse proxy with authentication while the update is not possible.
Check from outside your network that the port no longer answers, for example with `nc -vz 203.0.113.10 6379` or `nmap -Pn -p 6379 203.0.113.10` (replace the address and port with those of the finding).
Run the scan again: LeakIX rescans the host on its next passes, and the free plan returns results delayed by about 15 days; the finding can therefore stay displayed for a while after the fix.
module.leakix.fix_snippet:
# Redis (redis.conf)
bind 127.0.0.1 -::1
protected-mode yes

# MongoDB (mongod.conf)
net:
  bindIp: 127.0.0.1
security:
  authorization: enabled

# Elasticsearch (elasticsearch.yml)
network.host: 127.0.0.1
xpack.security.enabled: true

# PostgreSQL (postgresql.conf)
listen_addresses = 'localhost'

# MySQL / MariaDB (my.cnf)
[mysqld]
bind-address = 127.0.0.1

# ufw (Linux)
sudo ufw deny 6379/tcp
sudo ufw status numbered
module.leakix.title: LeakIX (exposed services and leaks)
module.leakix.why: A database or service left open without authentication is exploited by bots within hours; knowing it is indexed lets you close it first.
